notes:
Discovered in the 2026-10-21 trending crawl (HF trendingScore, text-generation filter; card created 2026-10-19, 62 likes, 0 downloads at read time, so this is a launch-week card, not a community-adopted one). Open weights, Apache-2.0, safetensors BF16, 5 shards.

PARAM DERIVATION: params_b 4.11 = safetensors.total 4,112,079,360 from api/models?blobs=true. Dense: config.json carries no expert/top_k/moe keys at all, so every token reads every weight and active_params_b = params_b. flops_per_token_active = 2 x 4.112e9 = 8.22e9. hidden_size 2560, intermediate_size 10240, 36 layers, vocab 131072, tied embeddings.

KV DERIVATION: layer_types read verbatim from config.json is 27 sliding_attention + 9 full_attention, full attention on indices 3,7,11,15,19,23,27,31,35 (every 4th layer starting at 3). kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 9 full-attention layers x 4 KV heads x head_dim 256 x 2 (K and V) x 2 B = 9 x 4 x 256 x 2 x 2 = 36,864 B/token (36 KiB) for the part that grows with context. The 27 sliding layers cap at window 512: 512 x 4 x 256 x 2 x 2 = 2,097,152 B (2.0 MiB) per layer, 27 x 2 MiB = 54 MiB of fixed per-sequence cache. So a full 1,048,576-token context costs ~36.9 GB of growing KV (1,048,576 x 36,864 B) plus 54 MiB - this is a sliding-window hybrid that divides KV by 4 (all-36-layer GQA would be 36 x 4 x 256 x 2 x 2 = 147,456 B/token), NOT a constant-state model. It does not bound memory growth.

HEAD GEOMETRY TRAP: 16 attention heads x head_dim 256 = a 4096-wide attention block over hidden_size 2560, so head_dim is not hidden_size/heads and gqa_ratio is 4 (16/4). rope_parameters are per layer type: full_attention uses partial_rotary_factor 0.25 with rope_theta 5,000,000 (64 of 256 dims rotated, the rest NoPE - and the cache still holds all 256 dims, so the partial rotary saves no KV), sliding_attention uses partial_rotary_factor 1.0 with rope_theta 10,000. headwise_attn_output_gate true, hidden_act gelu.

EVIDENCE: the card's benchmark table is an SVG (images/all_benchmark.svg), not markdown - the numbers below were extracted from its text nodes, and the SVG carries a 2026-10-21 render timestamp. Columns: Spark-X2.6-4B | Spark-X2.5-4B | Qwen3.5-9B | Qwen3.5-4B | Gemma4-12B | Gemma4-E4B. Card legend, verbatim: '* denotes reported results from publicly-released model cards / papers and - denotes scores not yet available'. So every Spark-X2.6 number is the vendor's own run; competitor cells with * are that competitor's own published number, not a Spark re-run. On the rows where no cell is starred (GPQA, tau^3-bench, BrowseComp, HLE w/o tools) all six models were run by Spark, which makes those the only genuinely same-harness comparisons on the card.

BEATS THE CATALOG'S 4B-CLASS BEST (same test names, vendor_claim on both sides): GPQA Diamond 77.1 vs qwen3-5-4b 76.2 (+0.9); TAU2-Bench 86.9 vs 79.9 (+7.0); IFBench 75.8 vs minicpm5-2b 66.3 and qwen3-5-4b 59.2; AA-LCR 67.3 vs qwen3-5-4b 57.0; SWE-bench Verified 62.8 vs nemotron-labs-dory1-4b 61.8 (+1.0, inside cross-harness noise); AIME 2026 91.2 vs minicpm5-2b 86.5. Card average 63.3 vs Qwen3.5-9B 49.1, Qwen3.5-4B 43.2, Gemma4-12B 47.0, Gemma4-E4B 29.7 - it beats models 2-3x its size on the aggregate, which is the size-class upset this record is for.

LOSES (recorded, not hidden): GPQA 69.9 vs Qwen3.5-9B 77.2 on the same-harness unstarred row - so the Diamond win over Qwen3.5-4B does not survive against the 9B. AA-LCR 67.3 vs Qwen3.5-9B 70.0*; LongBench v2 53.3 vs 55.2*; OpenAI-MRCR 512k-1M 26.0 vs Qwen3.5-9B 34.3 - long-context recall is where the 512-token sliding window shows. SciCode 36.8 vs Gemma4-12B 39.8; IFEval 93.6 vs Gemma4-12B 94.8; Gaokao 2026 134.9 vs Qwen3.5-9B 135.5. Card also prints tau^2-bench 86.9 beating every column, and SWE Pro 54.3 vs Qwen3.5-9B 33.8*.

CAVEATS: (1) all Spark numbers are vendor-run and none are third-party reproduced; (2) SWebBench 71.7 and the 'Average' row are excluded from benchmarks[] - SWebBench is the vendor's in-house benchmark, 'open-sourced soon', so it is not comparable across records, and Average is their own composite; (3) the card's own Qwen3.5-4B AA-LCR column prints 63.0*, while Qwen's own card (qwen3-5-4b) records 57.0 - a 6-point cross-card gap on the same named test, so quote the 57.0 comparison as directional; the 63.0 figure would still lose to Spark's 67.3; (4) HMMT is Feb 2026 here vs HMMT Feb 2025 74.0 in qwen3-5-4b, so that row is not a same-test comparison and no claim is made on it; (5) the catalog's 'GPQA' best for the class is nanbeige4-1-3b 83.8, above Spark's 69.9 - that row is on a different GPQA variant (its Diamond row is separate), so GPQA Diamond is the comparable test; (6) llama.cpp support is claimed for build b10828+ with a separate Spark-X2.6-4B-GGUF repo, which this crawl did not verify; (7) no KV-quant or long-context throughput numbers are published, so the 1M context is a configured ceiling, not a measured one.
